title: Set 152

sentences.ko: 아들이 수학 심화반으로 올라갔어요. 듣기엔 좋은데, 요즘 매일 집에 와서 반에서 자기가 제일 멍청하다고 해요. 그래서 그냥 원래 반에 두는 게 나았나 좀 고민돼요.
sentences.text: They moved my son up to the advanced math class, which sounds great, but now he comes home every day saying he's the dumbest kid in there. So I'm kind of wondering if we should've just left him where he was.

alts.text: So they bumped my kid up to advanced math, which sounds awesome, right? But now he comes home every day saying he's the dumbest one in there. Kinda makes me wonder if we should've just left him where he was.

My son has been moved up to the advanced mathematics class, which sounds wonderful; however, he now comes home every day saying that he is the least capable student in the class. I am therefore beginning to wonder whether we should have simply left him where he was.

sentences.note: **moved up** 은 반이나 등급을 위로 올린다는 뜻이에요. **I'm kind of wondering if** 는 확신은 없는데 좀 고민된다고 부드럽게 말할 때 써요. casual 의 **bumped my kid up** 도 같은 뜻이에요.

sentences.ko: 예전엔 일요일 축구가 정말 기다려졌는데, 젊은 애들이 나오기 시작하면서 다들 너무 이기려고만 해서 이제 아무도 재미가 없어요. 그래서 요즘은 그냥 핑계 대고 안 나가요.
sentences.text: I used to really look forward to our Sunday soccer games, but ever since those younger guys started showing up, it's gotten so competitive that nobody's having fun anymore. So lately I've just been making up excuses not to go.

alts.text: Man, I was always pumped for our Sunday soccer games, but ever since those younger guys started coming, it's gotten way too competitive and nobody's having fun anymore. So lately I've just been making up excuses to skip.

I once looked forward a great deal to our Sunday soccer games; however, since the younger players began attending, the games have become so competitive that no one enjoys them any longer. Consequently, I have recently been inventing excuses not to attend.

sentences.note: **look forward to** 는 무언가를 기다리며 설렌다는 뜻이에요. **making up excuses** 는 핑계를 지어낸다는 말이고, casual 의 **pumped** 는 잔뜩 신난 상태를 말해요.

sentences.ko: 뭔가 부러진 게 분명하다 싶어서 손목 때문에 병원에 갔는데, 의사가 그냥 삔 거래요. 그리고 장 본 걸 한 번에 다 들고 오려고 하지 말래요. 뭐, 맞는 말이죠.
sentences.text: I went in for my wrist because I was sure I'd broken something, but the doctor said it's just a sprain and that I should stop trying to carry all the groceries in one trip. Which, you know, fair.

alts.text: So I got my wrist checked since I was positive I broke something, but the doc says it's just a sprain and I gotta quit hauling all the groceries in one trip. Which, okay, fair.

I went to see the doctor about my wrist because I was certain I had broken something; however, the doctor said it is only a sprain and that I should stop attempting to carry all of the groceries in a single trip. That, admittedly, is a fair point.

sentences.note: **sprain** 은 삔 것, 염좌예요. 문장 끝 **Which, you know, fair.** 는 인정하기 싫지만 맞는 말이라고 받아들일 때 쓰는 구어체예요.
sentences.situation: 병원 갔다 온 얘기 가볍게 하기

sentences.ko: 회사에 고맙다는 말 하나 하려고 메일마다 전체 답장을 누르는 사람이 있는데, 오늘은 삼백 명쯤 받은 메일에 그걸 했어요. 별일 아닌 건 아는데, 진짜 받은편지함에 그 사람 이름이 한 번만 더 뜨면 폭발할 것 같아요.
sentences.text: There's this guy at work who hits reply all on every single email just to say thanks, and today he did it on one that went to like three hundred people. I know it's not a big deal, but I swear, if I see his name in my inbox one more time, I'm going to lose it.

alts.text: This one guy at work hits reply all on literally every email just to say thanks, and today he did it on one that went out to like three hundred people. Not a huge deal, I know, but I swear, if his name pops up in my inbox one more time, I'm gonna lose it.

There is a colleague at my workplace who replies to all recipients on every email merely to express his thanks, and today he did so on a message that had been sent to approximately three hundred people. I realize it is not a serious matter, but I must admit that if his name appears in my inbox once more, I will lose my patience.

sentences.note: **reply all** 은 전체 답장이에요. **lose it** 은 참다가 폭발한다, 이성을 잃는다는 뜻이에요. **I swear** 는 진짜, 맹세코처럼 말을 세게 할 때 붙여요.
sentences.situation: 회사 사람 때문에 짜증난 걸 친구한테 털어놓기

sentences.ko: 옆집에서 강아지를 들였는데, 매일 밤 열두 시쯤 낑낑 울어서 침실 벽 너머로 다 들려요. 강아지 가지고 불평하기는 좀 미안한데, 이번 주 내내 다섯 시간 넘게 자 본 적이 없어요.
sentences.text: Our neighbors got a puppy, and it cries every night around midnight, and I can hear it right through the bedroom wall. I feel bad complaining about a puppy, but I haven't slept more than five hours all week.

alts.text: So next door just got a puppy, and every night around midnight it starts crying and I can hear it right through the bedroom wall. Feels kinda bad to complain about a puppy, but I've been getting five hours of sleep, tops, all week.

Our neighbors have recently acquired a puppy, and it cries every night at approximately midnight; I can hear it clearly through the bedroom wall. I feel rather uncomfortable complaining about a puppy, but I have not slept more than five hours on any night this week.

sentences.note: **right through the bedroom wall** 은 벽을 뚫고 그대로 들린다는 느낌이에요. **I feel bad complaining** 은 불평하기 미안하다는 표현이고, casual 의 **tops** 는 많아 봤자라는 뜻이에요.

reviewed: 1번 casual 의 going he's the dumbest one 은 인용 going 뒤에 간접화법이 붙어 어색해서 saying 으로 바꿈
1번 note 의 bumped up 은 문장에 그대로 나오지 않아(bumped my kid up) 실제 나오는 형태로 고침
2번 한국어 '너무 승부욕 넘치게 돼서' 가 번역투라 '다들 너무 이기려고만 해서' 로 고침
5번 note 의 right through the wall 은 문장에 그대로 나오지 않아(right through the bedroom wall) 실제 나오는 형태로 고침
